title: Does a toothbrushing support app improve oral hygiene in children and young people?
official: Clara Trial A: a two-arm parallel study evaluating whether use of the Clara brushing-support app is associated with changes in plaque and gum-health measures in children aged 8–15 years
summary:
Background and study aims 
Dental caries (decay) and periodontal (gum) disease are highly prevalent diseases, with significant impacts on health and well-being. Effective removal of dental plaque by toothbrushing with a fluoride toothpaste can prevent or help control these two diseases. Apps have been shown to significantly improve the effectiveness of toothbrushing. This trial is a randomized controlled trial (RCT) of a novel mobile phone/tablet-based toothbrushing support app (Clara). This app provides coaching and reminders and monitors that toothbrushing has occurred across the mouth for the recommended 2 minutes, twice a day. Parents are notified if their child has not brushed effectively for 2 minutes twice a day in real time. For children, parents/carers can create a rewards structure within the app. This trial aims to investigate if use of the app is more effective than standard practice at the removal of dental plaque.

Who can participate? 
Healthy children aged 8-15 years who are patients of Hafren House Dental Practice, Alfreton, Derbyshire

What does the study involve? 
Participants will be randomly allocated into one of two groups (intervention or control). All participants will receive oral hygiene instruction, and those in the intervention group will also receive instruction in the use of the app. Plaque will be disclosed and recorded at the start of the study and at 4 weeks. Parents/carers and children will also report their experience of using the app and adverse events. 

What are the possible benefits and risks of participating? 
The benefits of participation are improved oral hygiene and reduced levels of tooth decay and gum disease. The risks include slight abrasion to the gums from brushing too vigorously and anxiety associated with the dental examination. This trial has the potential to identify a tool that can significantly improve dental health for all parts of the population.

Where is the study run from? 
Hafren House Dental Practice (UK)

When is the study starting and how long is it expected to run for?
August 2026 to March 2027

Who is funding the study? 
The Toothcare Project Ltd (UK)

interventions.name:
Participants will be randomised by computer-generated random number sequence into one of two arms:
Intervention: the use of the Clara Brushing support App on a mobile phone or tablet
Control: usual brushing routine

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
1. Aged 8–15 years inclusive at the time of consent
2. Attending Hafren House Dental Practice as a routine patient
3. Parent/guardian able and willing to give written informed consent
4. Child able and willing to give verbal assent (age-appropriate band: 8–12 or 13–15)
5. Access to a compatible device on which the Clara app can be installed (Clara arm only; eligibility confirmed prior to randomisation for both arms)
Exclusion criteria:
1. Acute oral health condition requiring urgent dental care at screening
2. Medical or developmental condition that, in the judgement of the site lead, would make participation unsafe or impracticable
3. Wearing a fixed or removable appliance is not an exclusion criteria
4. Concurrent participation in another oral-health interventional study
